summary: Susmita Basu Majumdar is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, where she later held a academic post and taught Smita Halder.

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Makio Takemura at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002). He held teaching posts at Kyoto University (~2008), Hanazono University (attested 2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (attested 2012–2013).

Susumu Shimazono is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and director at Sophia University (~2013–2021).

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University, the University of Paris, and Kyoto University, and served as a professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College, the University of London, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Toronto. He founded the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, serving as its president.

Suzanne Karpelès (1890–1968) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the EPHE and became a member of EFEO (1922–1925), first curator of the National Library of Cambodia (1925), and secretary-general of the Buddhist Institute (1930).
Suzanne Newcombe is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the Open University, Inform, and King's College London.

Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, the University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the University of Berlin under Ferdinand von Richthofen.
Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Swami Dayananda Saraswati (1930–2015) was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and under teachers including Chinmayananda Saraswati, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Veeraraghavachariar, and P. S. Subramania Iyer.
Swami Siddheswarananda (1897–1957) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras (~1916–1919) and served in the Ramakrishna Order (~1920–1957).

Swami Sivananda (1887–1963) was a figure in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Thanjavur Medical College (~1905–1909). He founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.
Swami Vimalananda (1872–1908) was a religious studies and philosophy figure. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.
Swami Vishnudevananda (1927–1993) was a religious studies and Indology figure. He studied as a disciple under Swami Sivananda (~1947–1957) and founded the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902) was a figure in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, and was a disciple of Ramakrishna (~1881–1886).

Sydney Frank Markham (1897–1975) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford (~1919–1923), and served as Secretary and later President of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).

Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Patna College, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and the Universities of Lucknow and London, later serving Hyderabad State and as Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (1901).

Syed Ameer Ali (1849–1928) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta, where he later held an academic post (~1875–1879).

Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Langat Singh College and Patna University, and served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali (1878–1958) was a scholar of history and archaeology. In 1932, he was attested as Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Principal of Bahauddin College.
